title: Shortcut Math (+= etc)
story: Every week, you drop a few coins into your piggy bank. Writing `savings = savings + 5` over and over feels clunky. What if there was a shorter, cooler way to say "add to this variable"? There is — meet `+=`!
why: Shortcut operators make code cleaner and are used in virtually every real program that updates values — from counters to animations to financial calculations.
analogy: Shortcut operators are like a remote control for your variable — one button press does the same thing as typing out the full command.
try_it: Start with 50, add 25 using `+=`, then subtract 10 using `-=`. Print after each step. Then try `*=` to double a number and `/=` to halve it!
tips: `x += 1` is a super common pattern — it's how you count things up one at a time!
Shortcut operators ONLY work with `var` — they change the value, which `let` doesn't allow
Think of `+=` as saying "bump up by" and `-=` as "knock down by" — it helps remember the order
common_mistakes: Writing `=+` instead of `+=` — the plus/minus always comes BEFORE the equals sign: `+=` not `=+`
Using shortcut operators with `let` variables — you'll get an error because `let` values can't change
